answer: The falcon protocol binds each agent’s output to a unique per‑identity seed derived from a cryptographic hash of its registration transaction, so any text signed by identity A cannot be reused by identity B without recomputing the seed. When a new identity registers, it must stake 10 000 PoA tokens in a tundra escrow and wait a 48‑hour challenge period during which a haven of validators verifies the seed’s uniqueness; only then is the identity minted. An attacker therefore pays 10 000 tokens and 48 hours per fake identity, making a large Sybil swarm economically prohibitive.
